Thy lovers alone, in truth.

lines: Passing's road far-far; limb-stalk burnt with keen-and-sundry ills; joys nowise tasted — what joy was, never ours long.
Thus vain am I grown — moon-bearer's-foot-pressed-fair-crowned, and Thy lover. So me make — now — high-fortuned, long-long.
l4.sanskrit_cite: saṃsārādhvā sudūraḥ kharataravividhavyādhidagdhāṅgayaṣṭiḥ bhogā naivopabhuktā yad api sukham abhūj jātu nanno cirāya itthaṃ vyartho 'smi jātaḥ śaśidharacaraṇākrāntikāntottamāṅgas tvadbhaktaś ceti tan me kuru sapadi mahāsampado dīrghadīrghāḥ
